title: Huntik Trading Card Game/Glossary
summary:
Term — Definition
Add X attacks — If a card instructs you to add a number of attacks to a combat, add that number to your team’s side of the combat.
ATK — Short for attack, the representation of a hero's combat prowess.
Control / Controller — You control all heroes on your team and may make plays with them during your turn. You also control any obstacles that specify they are controlled by you. Some cards and powers allow you to gain control of an opponent’s heroes. To gain control of an enemy hero, rotate it so it is right-side up from your point of view.
Counter — Some cards instruct you to place counters on a card in play and describe what those counters do. Any small objects (such as dice or beads) may be used as counters, but different types of counters should be clearly distinguished.
Deck — Your deck contains your heroes and Action cards at the start of the game. Shuffle your deck and draw 5 cards at the beginning of each game. Cards in your deck are face down, and you may not look through them.
DEF — Short for defense, the representation of a hero's protection level.
Defending hero — A defending hero is controlled by the defending player.
Discard — To discard a card, remove it from your hand and place it into your discard pile.
Discard pile — The discard pile contains heroes that have been KO’d or eliminated, Action cards after they are played, and cards discarded from hand. Leave space near your deck for your discard pile.
Draw — To draw a card, take the top card of your deck and put it into your hand.
Eliminate — When a hero is eliminated, remove it from the map and place it into its owner’s discard pile. You may only eliminate your own heroes.
Enemy — Enemy heroes are controlled by your opponent. Enemy attacks are aimed by your opponent.
Forceful — Attacks a hero adds to a combat cannot be removed.
Friendly — Friendly heroes are controlled by you.
Get — When a hero “gets” something, it gains that effect in addition to what is printed on its card. Example: “I get +1 ATK” adds 1 to the hero’s existing ATK. If a card states that heroes get a new power, treat the quoted power as if it were added to those heroes while the effect applies. Heroes retain all previously printed powers.
Hand — Your hand contains the cards you have drawn from your deck. Only you may look at the cards in your hand.
KO — Short for knock out, the state in which a hero is defeated in the game.
KO’d — When a hero is KO’d, remove it from the map and place it into its owner’s discard pile. When an obstacle is KO’d, remove it from the map.
Lead hero — A lead hero is controlled by the lead player.
My zone — When a hero card refers to “my zone,” it means the zone that hero is currently in. When an Exhaust Action card refers to “my zone,” it means the zone of the hero that played the Action.
Owner — You are the owner of any card that started the game in your deck. Whenever a card would be placed into a hand or discard pile, it is placed into its owner’s hand or discard pile.
Pick up — When a hero picks up an object, place the object underneath that hero. The object moves with the hero when the hero moves.
Printed — “Printed” refers to the text and values physically written on a card.
Reveal — To reveal a card, turn it face up so both players can see it. Afterward, return the card to its previous hidden state unless otherwise instructed.
Search — When instructed to search your deck for a specific type of card, look through your deck for a matching card, then shuffle your deck.
Stun — When a hero is stunned, exhaust it and turn it face down in its zone. A stunned hero cannot move, does not participate in combat, and cannot be targeted. If stunned during combat, remove its attacks from that combat. Attacks cannot be aimed at stunned heroes.
Target — When a card instructs you to target something, you must choose a valid target of the specified type. For example, if a card says “KO target major hero,” you must choose a major hero and may not choose a minor hero instead.
This zone — When a feature card refers to “this zone,” it means the zone in which that feature is located.
Unblockable — A hero cannot be prevented from moving by an opponent's hero being in a zone.
